translations.text: And again they force others like themselves to sacrifice and eat; and again they themselves offer sacrifices and force others to sacrifice others like themselves.
But he trusts in his idol, which is of no use.

He imagines that they created him, since they feed him and make him king, because of the blindness of his heart and his lack of understanding. For Satan has blinded his heart so that he does not recognize the God who created him, made him, and established him when neither he nor his possessions existed, so that he may go with Satan into judgment, and they may be condemned with him forever, together with those whom he called gods, although they are not gods.
And it is fitting to call them dead, for even now they are not alive.

As for those who trust in them, whose [?] is dust, the children of humankind, the spirit of Satan that deceives them enters into it with their idols. It speaks to them according to the desires of their hearts and appears to them as they wish.

When they see that he has fulfilled what they intended, they marvel and carry out his will, even to the point of slaughtering their sons and daughters who came from their wombs. They shed innocent blood, the blood of their sons and daughters.

They do not recoil from them, because Satan has made evil pleasing to them according to their desires, so that he may bring them down with him into his condemnation, the [?] of hell, from which there is no escape forever and ever.
Now Tsirutsaydan was arrogant, and he had [?] gods in male form and in female form.
There was a man from the people of Benjamin whose name was Maccabeus.
Some of them kill a bear by strangling it, at times strangling it like a chicken.
Some of them kill a lion with a single blow from a stone or with one stroke of a wooden club.
You examine the righteous and the sinner, and you search what is in the human heart. Nothing is concealed from you; even what is hidden is revealed before you.
But we have no other God besides you.
Only be our strength and firmness, and protect us in this work in which we serve you, so that we may save our lives from death for the sake of your holy name.
When Israel entered the land of Egypt, you heard Jacob’s prayer. Now we too ask you, holy God.
And when he appeared to them
Then they prayed, gave thanks, and bowed down to the Lord. Neither death nor the king’s judgment frightened them.
As King Tsirutsaydan sat in his court, he ordered them to bring those blessed ones, Abijah, Shelah, Phintos, and their mother, before him, bound and wounded.
Their younger brothers said, “We too will stand with you before the king, and if you die, we too will die with you.”
Then the king saw from the roof of his royal palace that those blessed ones had been released and were standing

They did as the king had commanded them and threw them into the sea. But the sea did not swallow them, even though they had placed heavy pieces of iron, large stones, and a donkey-driven millstone upon them. They did not sink into the sea but floated above the deep, because the Spirit of the Lord was upon them. He failed against them in every scheme he devised.
For days, eagles and birds sheltered them with their wings from the heat of the sun and brought them to [?]
They did so, and wild animals and birds did not touch their bodies, and their bodies remained
When they saw them, their bodies shone like the rays of the sun, and angels surrounded their bodies like a tent of light.
He deliberated but could not determine what to do. Then he dug into the ground and buried the bodies of the five martyrs.
He said to them, “What compensation shall I give you for the evil I did to you? For I did not know that this judgment would come upon me like this.
Now tell me how much compensation I should give you, so that you do not take my life by killing me or bring me down alive into Sheol.
For I have wronged you. Forgive this sin of mine, for your Father’s law is mercy.”
The blessed martyrs answered him and said, “We will not repay you with evil in return for what [?] did to us. The Lord our God is there to repay you, for vengeance belongs to the Lord.

But we have appeared to you to show that we are alive, because of the blindness of your heart and the deficiency of your understanding. Although you thought you had killed us, you prepared life for us.

Woe to you—you and your gods, whom you worship and bow down to! You have abandoned worship of the Lord who created you, although you are spittle and do not know where he brought you from. Are you not passing smoke, appearing now and vanishing tomorrow?
For your gods are gold and silver, wood and stone, the work of human hands. They have no soul, heart, or understanding.
Especially to those like you, whose hearts are blind, it seems that they created you, although you yourselves created them.
For the spirits of demons gather, and devils answer you as you wish, so that they may drown you in the sea of fire.
But you must abandon this error and worship the Lord our God. This will be our compensation for our death, so that we may gain a benefit for our souls.”
He was startled, astonished, amazed, and afraid, for sharp swords [?].
He said, “Now I know that the dead who have become dust truly rise again. And I [?] as one who has been spared from slaughter.”
Then they disappeared from the sight of that king. From that day, this Tsirutsaydan, who was proud and arrogant, stopped burning their bodies.

He rejoiced in the error of his heart and in his gods, for they had led him astray for many days. He was not the only one who went astray; he also led many others like himself astray, until they abandoned following their Creator.
He fed them with the produce of the fields and nourished them with honey from the rock, for he loved them greatly.
He also made you king over his people and gave you authority over four kingdoms, so that you would protect the people, shepherd them justly, and do the will of your Creator.
He made you king so that you would love the Lord your God all the more, for he exalted you above everyone and made you king.

It is right that you should love the Lord your God all the more, just as he loved you and entrusted you with his entire flock. Do the Lord’s will, so that your days on earth may be long and he may be with you.
He will triumph for you over all your enemies, establish you upon all your thrones, and spread his wings over your head.

If only you understood: the Lord chose you just as he chose Saul from the children of Israel and made him king over Israel, his people, while he was looking after his father’s donkeys; and he sat upon the throne with Samuel the prophet.
Nothing is hidden from his eyes; everything is revealed before him.
He is clothed in righteousness and justice and endowed with kindness and mercy.
He breaks the pride of the mighty who make widows and mortals weep.
He anointed David son of Jesse to reign in his place over Israel.
Samuel the prophet went to King Saul and entered his presence while he was standing at the table, with Agag, king of Amalek, on his left.

Again Saul said to Samuel, “Honor me before the people and intercede for me before God, so that he may have mercy on me.” But Samuel refused to go back on his word, because he feared the word of God his Creator and did not fear a mortal king.
Just as you strike without mercy those who commit wrongdoing, so you too have God to strike you and cast you into punishment from which there is no escape forever.
Just as you compel someone who has not paid you tribute and has not brought you a gift, why do you yourself not bring a gift to God?

And just as you want people to fear you, why do you not fear the Lord your God? For he is the one who created you and made you king over all his works, so that you might shepherd his people and his flock justly.

Do not turn aside either to the right or to the left, as Moses commanded the children of Israel, saying to them, “I have placed fire and water before you. Stretch out your hand toward whichever you choose.”

Listen to the voice of the one whom I appoint for you, so that you may hear his voice and carry out his commandment, and so that you do not say, “He is beyond the river. Who will bring him to me, so that I may see him and hear his voice and carry out God's commandment?”

And if you say again, “Who will go up to heaven for me and bring down that word from God's mouth, so that I may hear it and carry it out?” he said, “Look, the word is near you, in your mouth, and look, it is in your hand.”
If you have not listened to the scripture, you have not listened to the Lord your God. And if you have not kept my word, you have not loved him, and you have [?] his commandment.

You are destined to enter eternal punishment, because you have not loved his commandment or done the will of the one who made you great and honored you above all your people, so that you might shepherd them in your righteousness.
He made you exalted and head over all his people, while you remember the name of your God, who created you and granted you authority to govern the people with justice and uprightness.
Barley. And if you sow cumin, will you harvest [?]? And among trees, if you plant a fig tree, will it produce almonds? And if you plant a walnut tree, will it produce grapes for you?
Likewise, unless the dew of life comes down upon them from God, the dead will not rise.
The lowlands of Gilboa and the mountains of Lebanon do not produce grass for livestock and wild animals when the rain of mercy does not come down upon them from God.
The mountains of Gilead and the lowlands of Elam do not give green vegetation to the goats and lambs that graze there, or to the wild animals, [?], wild oxen, and deer.

Likewise, rebels and heretics who previously acquired rebellion and error will not rise from the dead unless the dew of mercy comes down upon them from God, nor will deceivers and sorcerers, practitioners of [?] and [?].
And those who practice sorcery and magic, and murderers.
And those who commit unlawful sexual acts, and the Athenians and Medes who trust in their idols, sing to them, and make music for them with drums, stringed instruments, and harps.
They act madly with their idols and commit adultery with the works of their own hands, which cannot save themselves and will themselves be condemned on the day of judgment, at the resurrection.
You foolish and feeble-minded person, do you think that the dead will not rise?
Do not think this way, for you will not sleep there when the horn is blown at the resurrection of the dead by the mouth of Michael, the archangel.
And you too, do not let your mind go astray, saying, “How will the dead rise after they have died, those who are placed [?] in—”
And she entered the grave and became dust, like her forefathers, who went their own way and rejected God's commandment, so that at the resurrection he would take vengeance on them.
Their wine is the venom of the serpents of the earth, the deadly poison of vipers.

This is your disgrace, daughter of Jerusalem, which was written by the prophet: just like the deeds and sins of the people of Sodom and Gomorrah, so are your deeds and your sins, daughter of Jerusalem.
And when it bore fruit and was pressed, it became a source of corruption and punishment. It hardens the hearts of those who drink it and consigns them to cold, far from God.
And a dwelling place for the devil, because they walk in his evil ways. The vine of Sodom takes hold, devouring, and climbs into the mountains and into the trees.

I too will mock you and will not hurry to save you, because you rejected my word and did not persevere in my counsel: that you should walk with me and keep my commandments, and that I should be with you and save you from all who oppose you, while you kept the commandments I gave you and my ordinances.

You did not keep any of this, and I too mocked you. At the time of judgment I will take vengeance on you. Was it not I who created you? Yet you did not keep my word and my commandments, though I blessed you so that you would be mine.
But you withdrew from me, just as Sodom and Gomorrah withdrew.

I struck them in my wrath, for you are of the stock of Sodom and Gomorrah, whom I destroyed. I wiped their memory from the earth so that they would not persist in their indecency, because they provoked me, their creator, by going to a man's wife and having unlawful intercourse with males and animals as with women.

There is no fear of God before their eyes, from the least of them to the greatest. No one rebukes another so that he will refrain from doing it [?]. They help them in every evil deed and are filled with every injustice and lust, for their deeds are evil.
Every evil deed is established in their minds, along with pride, arrogance, and greed.
Because of this, God mocked them and devastated their cities. Some he burned with fire down to their foundations, and nothing remained within them. They perished and were destroyed forever.

It will remain until the day of judgment, forever, and until the great day of judgment, because they were bound by sin. He will not forgive them or have mercy on them, because they provoked me by their evil deeds.

I too mocked them. Likewise you, disgraced daughter of Jerusalem, will be bound on the day of judgment, for you will find no excuse when I seize you in my wrath. All your deeds are filth, arrogance, greed, sexual immorality, lying speech, and every path of error and stumbling that I do not approve.
I appointed you for honor, but you appointed yourself for disgrace. While I called you mine, you gave yourself to another.

I will prolong severe vengeance against you because of all your failure to listen to my word and keep the commandments I gave you on the day I loved you. For I am God, who created you, and I will be angry with all sinners who are like you. On the day of judgment I will repay them according to their wickedness.

Woe then to those who obey the unclean ones and offer sacrifices in their names, because they rebel against God who created them and become like animals without understanding. For that wicked one, the son of destruction, sets up his images in every place and rejoices in the work of his hands, in his soul's desire, and in every lust, arrogance, injustice, and deceit, and in everyone who practices sexual immorality, arrogance, and falsehood.

The sun will be darkened, the moon will become blood, and the stars will fall from heaven. Every work will perish through the sign that will come in the last days, to judge the earth and everything in it according to the deeds of those who inhabit it.
Vengeance will be exacted for widows and orphans, because he is the defender and avenger of those who are oppressed by the hand of their oppressors.
They run toward this evil all the days of their lives. The children of Israel, who transgress the commandments of God, provoked God still more, from the first to the last.
At Horeb too, the children of Israel provoked God by making a calf that grazes on grass. They bowed down and said, “Here are our gods who brought us out of the land of Egypt.”

Moses said to Joshua, “It is not the sound of battle, but the sound of revelry over wine.” He went down and shattered their image, grinding it by scraping until it became like dust. He put it into the spring from which the children of Israel drank, at the foot of the mountain.
They did as he commanded them, knowing that reproach against God was greater than the killing of themselves or the killing of their relatives and fathers.
Because of this, God gave strength to three brothers. Their names were Mebecius, Maccabeus, and Judas. They were handsome in appearance and mighty in all their strength.
Those good and handsome brothers prepared to go and save them. They took counsel together and said to one another, “Let us go and give our lives to death for these people.”

They fell and died, and they left everything they owned until they crossed the Jordan. Everything they owned remained behind. When the children of Israel saw that they had departed and gone away with their [?], they took their plunder for themselves.

And afterward [?] they returned again to their wickedness, and the children of Israel ceased to worship God sincerely. He again afflicted them through a people [?] who harvested the produce of their fields, ruined their vineyards, took their pastures, and slaughtered their cattle before their eyes. They could not save them, because they were a people who transgressed the law, continually provoking God at all times.

Do not show favoritism to anyone, or be robbers, oppressors, abusers, men who go to another man's wife, people who do evil and violence to their neighbors, or people who conspire unjustly to oppress their neighbors.
They quarrel, join themselves together, and swear together to do evil. They hurry to lead people astray, to bring them down into the condemnation of eternal judgment.
Remember that you are going to God, and that everything is in his hand. You will stand before him to be judged for the deeds you have done.

For in the same way, long ago, the children of the Watchers were wicked and arrogant. No one was greater or stronger than they were in stature and in the strength of their arms. Yet they did not keep God before their eyes or acknowledge that he was their Creator, who brought them into being when they did not exist.
Their fathers, being angels, used to offer praise with the angels in heaven. But when their desire led them astray, they descended into the condemnation of eternal judgment.

They took wives from among human beings, for God created human flesh for them to bring them into subjection because of the pride of their hearts, and to test whether they would keep his commandment and his law.
Likewise, the angels who went astray with the daughters of Cain drew us into their error. Because of this, the days God gave us were shortened in comparison with the days of our fathers.
Their offspring will increase upon the earth, and their memory will remain good forever. Their seed will not cease to bear grain upon the earth.
But those who did not trust in God and trusted instead in the abundance of their wealth were deprived of the grace he had given them, for God shows no favoritism.
God does this for the one he loves, but the one he hates he makes a captive of his enemy.
As for those who do good, he was commanded by God to repay them with good things and to protect them by his own hand.

He too must keep the commandment, for he is a messenger over everything that God created, to do good and give them eternal life. They praise God, who created them. Of all that he created, none transgresses his commandment except human beings alone.
They all acknowledge him and observe his commandment and his order, just as God commanded all of them to remain in their appointed order.
But the human being transgresses against the one who made him king over all the wild animals and livestock, and over all the birds that God created.

Whether in the sea or on dry land, everything God created he entrusted to our father Adam, so that he might do as he wished, eat them as he ate the plants of the earth, possess them, and make them serve him. Whether wild animals or livestock, God gave them over to obey human beings. And the human beings who were made kings were to obey God: because he gave them honor and appointed them over everything he created, they were to be faithful to him and obey him.
He accepts the petitions of those who ask him and of the one who does his will with a pure heart. He hears their prayers and fulfills their wishes in everything they ask of him.
But God's wrath is against those who do evil, to erase their memory from the earth. He will leave no one who boasts [?], either in the mountains or in resting places.
A fearful command will be pronounced against them, saying, “Cast them into the punishment of blazing fire, where there is no escape forever.”
God, who rules everything, said, “Save yourselves from idols, magicians, and diviners.”
Their kings too are troublemakers who rush to do evil, for they disregard the cries of the poor and needy and do not rescue foreigners from the hands of those who abuse them.

Woe to their souls when God seizes them in his wrath because they did not set their conduct right during their lives! They will perish quickly, like someone who leaves his hiding place, whose tracks cannot be found, and who does not return to his house.

Their stores of grain and their clothing will be consumed [?] by moths and worms. Everything passes away like yesterday, the day that has passed. As a word that has come out of the mouth does not return, so is the wealth of sinners. As a shadow passes away, so does the splendor of their possessions. Like a worn-out garment, so is the wealth of sinners before God.

But as for the righteous, even if they are wealthy, God does not disregard them, because they show compassion to the poor with their wealth, uphold justice for orphans and the needy, clothe the naked from their own clothing, and do not withhold the produce of their household that God gave them to give to foreigners and the needy.

They must not pervert justice for the faithful, withhold a hired worker's wages, or commit injustice in the reckoning of their months or in the measures of their scales. For righteousness and the honored word of God are like one who fills [?].

And the poor, in turn, ponder on their beds. If the rich do not receive them, they become like a dry tree that has no moisture. Where there is no moisture, its root does not sprout, and when it has no root, no leaf sprouts.
And if no leaf sprouts, it produces no fruit, because the leaf serves the growth of the fruit. Whoever has no fruit has no good deeds, for a man's head is the fruit of righteousness.
And if he practices righteousness, he bears the fruit of uprightness. God rejoices in the person who practices righteousness and uprightness.
He grants the prayer of the one who prays and the reward of his lips. He does not oppress the righteous person because of the righteousness he has practiced.

And whoever declares a sinner righteous without repentance for the evil deeds he has done [?]. For God is righteous and loves righteousness. In judgment he shows favor neither to the rich nor to the poor, for he is the ruler of heaven and earth, and the life of everyone is in his hands.

He created the whole world out of nothing. He prepared and established the mountains and rocks, and made the earth firm upon the water. He enclosed it with sand so that it would not shake, for God's first word was, "Let there be light."
He spread it out like sackcloth and supported it with wind. He made the lower [?] water dwell beneath the depths of the sea.

He closes the gates of the sea with sand and makes them firm by his spirit so that they do not sink into the depths below. He made wild beasts and animals dwell within it, and great animals within it, beyond counting, both those that are visible and those that are invisible.
On the third day God made plants upon the dry land, and all the grass and trees, each according to its kind, and the fruits they bear.

And the tree of life, beautiful to look at and sweet to eat, and grass and all the green plants of the earth that have their seed within them. He appointed them as food for all animals, wild beasts, and birds, and gave nourishment to everything he had created.

There was evening, and morning came. On the fourth day God said, "Let there be light in the expanse of heaven." God made the sun, the moon, and the stars, and placed them in the expanse of heaven to shine upon the earth and to rule over it by day and by night.
They worshiped idols according to their customs until righteous Abraham came forth, who did the will of God.
And their descendants after them, the children of Jacob, he made kings and priests from [?] the lineage of the people of Israel. He blessed them and said to them, "Increase and multiply abundantly."
He stretches out his right hand in blessing to satisfy the hungry soul. He opens his eyes in mercy and increases the grain for nourishment.
But again they turn to provoking him, and he sends against them nations and their enemies who surround them. They destroy them, kill them, and take them captive.
Again they cry out to God with lamentation and tears, and he sends them help. Sometimes he saved them through the prophets.
At other times he saved them through the judges. When they provoked God, their enemies enslaved them, plundered them, and [?].
David arose and saved them from the power of the Philistines. Again they provoked God, and he sent against them those who would oppress them.

At one time he saved them through Jephthah. Again they forgot God, who had saved them, and he sent against them wicked enemies who tormented them, took them captive, and plundered them, for God was repaying them.
Again they cried out to him when they were oppressed, and he saved them through Gideon. Again they provoked God by the works of their hands.
He again sent them those who would torment them. They returned, wept, and cried out to God.
Again he saved them through Samson, and they rested for a short while. Then they arose to provoke God with the evil they had practiced before.
He again sent them others who would oppress them. Again they cried out and wept before God so that he would send them [?], and he saved them through Deborah and Barak.
Again they spent a few days worshiping God. Then they again forgot God and provoked him with their former evil.
He sent them others who would oppress them, and again he saved them through Judith. Again they remained for a little while, then arose to provoke God with their evil as before.
And he raised up for them men who would rule the nations. They cried out and pleaded with the Lord, and he saved them through Mattathias and his sons, on the corner of the house.
Esther also said, “Fast, pray, and cry out to the Lord, the God of Israel, all you assemblies of the children of Israel, wherever you are.”

Esther mourned deeply. Although she was queen, she wore sackcloth, spread ashes, shaved her head, and did not anoint herself with perfume as the queens of Persia did. She wept and cried out from the depths of her heart to the Lord, the God of her ancestors.
Because of this, the Lord granted her favor before Artaxerxes, king of Persia, and she held a great feast for the God of her ancestors.
“Be good to me, and I too will be good to you. Keep my commandments, and I too will preserve your lives. Walk according to my commandments, and I too will act according to your hearts’ desires.
Love me, and I too will love your lives. Take refuge in me, and I too will strengthen you.
Trust in me, and I too will save you,” says the Lord who rules over all.

“Do not wander this way and that. Draw near to me, and I will draw you near, for I love upright paths,” says the Lord who rules over all. “Cleanse your hands, you sinners and evildoers, and remove the evil from your hearts.
And I too will remove my wrath from you and turn toward you with compassion and mercy.”
And he spoke, as he spoke to Eli, the elderly priest whose conduct was good, and to Samuel the prophet while he served in the house of the Lord God.

When he grew up serving in the house of the Lord, he appointed him to appoint the people and anoint kings at the Lord’s command. He entrusted the royal anointing to his hands when he did the will of the Lord his God, because he was pleasing in his sight, so that he might establish kings over the people whom the Lord had chosen from the children of Israel.
While Saul was reigning, the Lord said to Samuel the prophet, “Go and anoint David, the son of Jesse, from the house of Judah, for I am pleased with him.
I have hated the house of Saul, because he provoked me by transgressing my word.
And I too have rejected him. No one from his house will reign again, because he did not keep my word.
Likewise, from those who have not kept my word and do not walk according to my law and my ordinances, I will withhold my gifts, and I will withhold my kingdom from their descendants forever.
I will change my mind and not exalt them again, but will only destroy them. For when I exalted them, they did not exalt me, and when I honored them, they did not honor me.
When I was good to them, they were not good to me, and when I showed them mercy, they did not show me mercy.
For I made them the head over everyone, but they did not make me the head over them. When I honored them above everyone, they did not honor me or keep my commandments.
I am the one who shows compassion to those who love me and remember my name at all times. For the poor and the rich, I am the provider of food.

And you, kings and rulers, listen to my word and keep my commandments,” says the Lord who rules over all. “The children of Israel rebelled against me and worshiped other gods, although I am the Lord their God, who protected them, saved them, made them greater than their ancestors, and fed them with everything they desired.
I also fed them manna, bread in the wilderness, as David said, ‘Human beings ate the bread of his angels.’ I did all this for them so that they would worship me in righteousness and uprightness.
But they did not worship me, and I too despised them,” says the Lord who rules over all. “They rebelled against me and walked on a path that was not mine.

I too will repay them according to their conduct, and I have despised them according to the work of their hands, because they despised worshiping me and did not persevere in my ordinances and my counsel. I will bring them down under the condemnation of the judgment in heaven.
On earth too I will shorten their days, because they did not keep my commandments, and I too will rebel against them.
And you, king, are you not a human being who will die and decay, who tomorrow will become moths and worms and dust?
And now you boast and grow proud, as though you will never die.
Brother will rise against brother, and the Lord will exact vengeance, as he said concerning them, so that they perish.
And those who live on the islands of Arabia, India, Nubia, Sheba, Egypt, and Ethiopia, and all who live on them.
Then they will know that I am the Lord who rules heaven and earth, and that I am the one who gives honor and favor, and I am the one who kills and gives life.
And I am the one who makes the sun rise and sends it to its setting, and I am the one who brings good and evil.
And I am the one who brings a people you do not know, who will consume the fruit of your labor and the pastures of your cattle and sheep.

They will [?] your children before you and take them captive, and you will be unable to save them. They will consume the fruits of your toil and your lush growth, because you did not fear the commandment of the Lord that you heard, because the Spirit of the Lord did not increase upon you.
As gold and silver are tested by fire, so sinners will be tested on the last day, because they did not keep the commandment of the Lord.
It became a place of confusion and desolation; it became [?] and a wilderness, and wild beasts dwell within it.
Then you will be repaid according to the work of your hands. Why do you exalt your heart and stretch out your neck? says the Lord who rules over all.
If you do the will of the Lord and walk in his commandments, he will love you, so that you may rejoice with him in his kingdom and have a share with those who have inherited the holy city.
And again they will return and set out and cry out to the Lord their God.

But the souls of the righteous from the descendants of the children of Israel are like bright stars in the heights of heaven. For the Lord said to Abraham, “Look at the sky at night and count the stars of heaven, if you can count them. In the same way, your righteous descendants will shine like stars in the kingdom of heaven.”
